items.item: Strong Fiscal Performance and Tax Collection
items.explanation: Overperforming revenues and tighter-than-budgeted fiscal execution provide fiscal space, supporting fiscal consolidation and medium-term debt reduction targets.
items.evidence_quote: Fiscal performance in the first half of 2024 was tighter than budgeted, driven by robust tax collection.

items.explanation: FDI inflows help cushion the overall balance of payments despite an expanding current account deficit caused by tourism sector softening.
items.evidence_quote: However, an influx of FDI related to the development of Assumption Island (Seychelles is an archipelago of 115 islands, only some of which are developed) is expected to lead to an improvement in the overall balance of payments in 2024.

items.explanation: Adequate and rising gross international reserves strengthen external stability and provide a buffer against external balance of payments shocks.
items.evidence_quote: Nonetheless, gross international reserves rose to $754 million by August 2024, equivalent to 3.5 months of import cover.

items.explanation: Healthy bank capital and liquidity indicators limit systemic financial sector contagion and maintain core domestic financial stability.
items.evidence_quote: Commercial banks remain well capitalized, liquid, and profitable (Table 5). NPLs as a share of gross loans decreased from 8.2 percent at end-2023 to 7.2 percent in June 2024

items.explanation: Consistently meeting program quantitative criteria establishes policy credibility and anchors macroeconomic stability.
items.evidence_quote: All end-June 2024 quantitative performance criteria (QPCs) and all end-September 2024 indicative targets (ITs) were met.

items.explanation: A downward medium-term debt trajectory supported by structural fiscal consolidation keeps domestic and balance of payments financing risks manageable.
items.evidence_quote: Financing needs have decreased since 2020, and public debt has been assessed as sustainable with high probability.

items.item: Slowdown in Tourism Demand and Tourist Spending
items.explanation: Economic growth remains vulnerable to shocks in tourism, which directly affects GDP, tax receipts, and foreign exchange receipts.
items.evidence_quote: Economic growth in Seychelles appears to have slowed relative to earlier forecasts, reflecting lower tourist arrivals and lower tourist spending in Q2 and Q3.

items.item: High Import Dependency and Commodity Price Exposure
items.explanation: Heavy reliance on imported fuel, food, and goods leaves inflation and external balances vulnerable to exchange rate depreciation and global price shocks.
items.evidence_quote: Average annual inflation is projected to stabilize at around 3 percent over the medium term but remains subject to external shocks and currency movements given Seychelles' high import dependency.

items.explanation: Substantial structural current account shortfalls expose the country to external payment pressures if financing flows decelerate.
items.evidence_quote: Despite an increase in tuna and other exports, the external current account deficit is expected to widen to 10.7 percent of GDP in 2024, from 7.2 percent of GDP in 2023.

items.explanation: Persistently wide banking spreads inflate borrowing costs, curtailing credit access, financial inclusion, and medium-term private investment.
items.evidence_quote: High borrowing costs generated by the banks' large interest rate spread may limit private credit and hamper medium-term growth (Annex II).

items.explanation: Sea-level rise and extreme weather threaten critical coastal tourism assets and physical infrastructure, while transition costs pose immense financing needs.
items.evidence_quote: Seychelles remains vulnerable to sea level rise and natural disasters via damage to coastal infrastructure and tourism.

items.explanation: High levels of non-performing loans, largely concentrated in a single institution and the tourism sector, present ongoing financial stability vulnerabilities.
items.evidence_quote: NPLs are largely concentrated in the tourism sector-a consequence of the COVID pandemic-and mostly affect a specific bank.

judge.rationale: The candidate provides an exceptionally accurate and well-balanced synthesis of the primary macroeconomic strengths and vulnerabilities detailed in the report. Every claim is strictly supported by the text without contradictions.
